parentLineId.description: For an add-on attaching to a ticket already in the cart. **Removing the parent removes the child** — a locker with no admission is not a sale.

token.description: **How an anonymous guest returns to their cart**, including from a recovery email. Rotated on claim, so a link shared before signing in does not reach the account after.

appliedPromotionIds.description: **Re-evaluated on every read.** A promotion that expired while the cart sat must not still be applied at checkout, and a promotion that became applicable should be.

expiresAt.description: The earliest lease expiry in the cart, or the cart's own window where it holds none.

CartConflict.description: 2.9.5. Golf at 13:00 and karting at 13:00 for the same guest. **A prompt, not a refusal** — a party of four may legitimately split, and refusing would be wrong more often than right.

isBlocking.description: Most are not. `requiresPrerequisite` is — an add-on with no ticket to attach to cannot be sold.

overrideReason.description:
BL-085. **An operator could apply an approved discount and not enter a price.** A price match against a competitor and a service-recovery gesture are not discounts off a list — they are a number somebody decided.
**Escalated above a configured threshold, and the reason is a closed set**: a free-text override reason is an override nobody can report on, and this is the field an auditor reads first.

feeKind.description:
**A fee is a line, not an adjustment.** `orders` already separates a service charge from a tip for the reason that applies here: **a guest is entitled to see what they are being charged for**, and a fee folded into the ticket price is a fee nobody can question.
Itemised at checkout, taxed on its own code, and refundable separately — **a cancellation fee is usually the one thing not refunded**, which only works if it is its own line.

inventoryHoldId.description: The capacity held for this line. **Null for a product with no capacity** — a t-shirt needs stock, not a lease.

leaseExpiresAt.description: Shown to the guest. *"Your seats are held for 6 minutes"* is better than discovering it at checkout.

isAvailable.description: Re-checked on every read. **A line can become unavailable while the cart sits** — a lease expiring is not the same as the product selling out, and both land here.

CommissionStatement.x-ticvai-persistence: none — aggregated from orders and control.partner_agreement

lines.description: **Reconcilable order by order.** A statement a partner cannot check line by line is a statement they will dispute, and the dispute costs more than the detail.

agreementVersion.description: The version in force at the time of that sale, not the current one.

combinedDiscount.description: Combined percentage where both apply to the same line.

isBlocking.description: True where the combination would produce a negative or near-zero price.

worstCaseDiscount.description: Largest combined discount any single line could receive.

inventoryHoldId.description: Lease the units were drawn from. Absent for uncontended products.

seatIds.description: Seated products only. Not available offline.

quotedUnitPrice.description: What the client charged, from its local bundle.

id.description: Client-generated ULID. Also the idempotency key.

subjectId.description: Null for an anonymous sale. Identity and entitlement are separate.

guestLinkId.description: Present where the guest is linked across cells.

catalogueBundleVersion.description: The bundle the client priced from. Lets the server explain a variance rather than merely report one.

precedence.description: Higher evaluates first where several could apply.

budgetCap.description: Total discount value after which the promotion stops automatically.

lineIds.description: Omit to refund the whole order.

secondaryAuthorisation.description: Required above the venue's `requiresSecondUserAbove`. A second user — cashier or supervisor — names themselves. This is dual-authorisation, not escalation.

releaseAt.description: Automatic release, for production holds freed close to performance.

evaluateAt.description: For back-office testing of a rule before publishing.

lineId.description: Omit to discount the order rather than a line.

reason.description: Required, and free text rather than a code list. A cashier forced to pick the nearest reason picks the first one, and the register stops meaning anything.

reasonCode.description: Optional alongside the free text, where the venue maintains a list.

approverPrincipalId.description: Required above the venue threshold. May not be the requester.

channel.description: Where it came from. Drives revenue attribution, promotion eligibility and the self-service adoption figures the operator will ask for within a month of launch.

currency.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else. **Kept on the wire , removed from the table** — a client should not walk a hierarchy to read a figure, and the  database should not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their
 region and keep a stored currency: `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, 
`ledger.account`, `control.partner_agreement`.

count`, `control.partner_agreement`. **A guest paying USD at an AED venue is a real row; a w orkstation with its own currency is a misconfiguration.**

totalPriceVariance.description: Sum across lines. Zero on a normal order.

OrderChannel.description: Where the order originated. Added when guest self-ordering was contracted — an order a guest placed on their own phone is commercially and operationally different from one a cashier typed, and reporting that cannot separate them cannot answer whether self-ordering is working.

difference.description: Only the difference settles. The replacement is held before the original is released, never the other way round.

serverUnitPrice.description: What the server computed on ingest.

priceVariance.description: Server minus quoted. Non-zero means the quoted price was honoured and the difference posted to the variance account.

crossRegionRightIds.description: Redemption rights propagated to other cells for this line.

balanceDue.description: Positive means the guest pays; negative means a refund is due.

hasChanged.description: True where anything moved while the sale was parked. The cashier decides — silently charging the old price loses money, silently charging the new one loses the guest.

OrderStatement.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from order, payment, refund and ledger

entries.description: Sequential. What an agent reads to a guest asking about a charge.

currentBalance.description: Positive means the guest owes; negative means a refund is outstanding.

OrderStatus.description: `held` is a parked sale — the cashier freed the till and the guest will return. It holds no inventory and expires, because a till that accumulates parked sales across a shift cannot be closed.

version.description: **Amending creates a version.** An order placed last week was placed under last week's rate, and settlement must be able to say which.

volumeTiers.description:
2.7.57. **A tier that changes at a threshold needs the sale to look back at cumulative volume, and nothing did.** Flat net rates and per-channel price lists cover the simple case and stop there.
**The window is the argument, not the tier.** A partner who sells 400 in January and 400 in February is either a 400-tier partner twice or an 800-tier partner once, and the two are different money. `volumeWindow` says which.

appliesRetrospectively.description: **Whether crossing a tier reprices what came before it.** Retrospective is what a partner assumes and prospective is what a venue budgets for — it has to be stated.

seasonalRates.description: Rates that change by date range. **Separate from the volume tier because they compound** — a peak-season rate at a high volume tier is both, and a single rate table cannot say so.

brandingAssetId.description:
2.7.x, BL-078. **A reseller selling a venue's tickets under their own brand is a second scope level white-label does not have** — `BrandIdentity` and `setTheme` are tenant-scoped throughout.
**Co-branding rather than replacement.** The venue's identity stays on the ticket because the ticket admits to the venue; the partner's sits beside it.

sponsorship.description:
BL-050. **Sponsorship inventory is sellable capacity of a different kind** — logo placements, hospitality allocations, naming rights. It is closer to a partner agreement than to a product: **a sponsor buys a relationship for a season, not a ticket for a date.**
Modelled here rather than as a `ProductKind` because the commercial terms — the term, the exclusivity, the settlement — are the agreement's, and duplicating them onto a product would mean two places to disagree.

exclusive.description: **Exclusivity is the expensive word.** A sponsor paying for category exclusivity has bought the absence of a competitor, and a second agreement breaching it is a legal problem rather than a scheduling one.

hospitalityAllocation.description: Tickets or cabanas included. **Issued as invitations, not sales** — no revenue attaches.

netRates.description: Per product or category. Absent means the commission applies across the catalogue.

maxDiscountPercent.description: 1.6.10. **What the partner may not undercut.** A reseller selling below the venue's own price damages the direct channel, and the venue usually cares more about that than the margin.

creditTermDays.description: 2.7.36. Net 30, net 60. Drives when an invoice becomes overdue.

acceptedByPrincipalId.description: BL-079. **Electronic acceptance against a version**, following the `signatureRef` precedent. An agreement accepted with no version recorded is an agreement nobody can produce in a dispute.

corporateAllocations.description: BL-035. **`PartnerAgreement` covered commercial terms and not allocations.** A corporate account with fifty places for its staff is the same structure as a reseller with fifty to sell, and **the difference is that a corporate member does not pay.**

settlementCurrency.description:
**The currency this partner is billed and settles in**, which is often not the venue's. A UK tour operator selling a Dubai attraction is invoiced in GBP against sales booked in AED, and the difference is somebody's exposure.
**`creditLimit` and `netRates` are expressed in this currency**, not the venue's — a limit in the wrong currency is a limit that moves with the exchange rate.

fxPolicy.description:
**Which rate converts a sale into the settlement currency, and it is a commercial term.** `rateAtSale` puts the movement on the partner; `rateAtInvoice` puts it on the venue; `fixedRate` puts it on whoever guessed wrong when the agreement was signed.
**Not a default to leave alone** — on a monthly statement across a moving rate the three produce materially different numbers, and the partner will have assumed one of them.

fixedRate.description: Where `fxPolicy` is `fixedRate`. **An amendment creates a version** so an old statement stays readable.

requiresApprovalAboveValue.description: 2.7.39. Routes through `approvals` rather than a second mechanism here.

validTo.description: 2.7.37. **An agreement that lapses silently keeps selling at rates nobody agreed to**, discovered at settlement rather than at sale. Null means open-ended, which should be rare and deliberate.

PartnerQuote.description: **Drafted 4 September.** A priced offer to a partner, with an expiry. **Not the same as a procurement quotation** - `inventory.quotation` is what a supplier offers this venue, and this is what this venue offers a reseller.

currency.description: **Not stored on the row.** Currency is region-scoped and resolves from the scope walk (ADR-0018); a quote that carries its own copy is a quote that disagrees with the region the moment one of them changes.

validUntil.description: **Stored, not calculated** - an offer whose expiry moves when you read it is not an offer.

PartnerRateMode.description: **Alternatives, not both.** A partner buys at a net rate and keeps the margin, or sells at face value and is paid commission. Both is being paid twice for the same sale.

tenderCurrency.description:
4.6.11. **What the guest actually handed over**, which is not always what the venue books. A tourist paying USD cash at a till is a foreign tender; the sale is still recorded in base currency.
Equal to the base currency for almost every payment. **Present on all of them so the foreign-tender report has a source** — `getForeignTenderReport` promised *what was taken in which currency* and nothing recorded it until 18 August.

tenderAmount.description: The amount in `tenderCurrency`, at that currency's own scale.

fxRate.description: The rate applied, **stored on the payment rather than looked up later** (CF-37). A payment reconciled next month is reconciled at the rate of the day it was taken.

fxRateSource.description: 4.2.8. Manual or fed on a schedule. **`cardScheme` is where the terminal did the conversion and told us** — dynamic currency conversion, the scheme's rate rather than ours.

changeCurrency.description: 4.6.11 is deliberately asymmetric: **accept foreign currency, refund in local.** A till giving change in five currencies needs five floats and five counts, and the variance becomes unattributable.

rejected.description: Promotions that matched the products but did not apply, with the reason. This is what a cashier reads to a guest who expected a discount.

PromotionUsage.x-ticvai-persistence: none — aggregated from ledger and orders

fxRate.description:
**The rate on the original payment, not today's** (BL-087, CF-118).
`Payment` records `tenderCurrency`, `fxRate` and `fxRateSource` at the moment of sale, so the sale rate is always retrievable. **Refunding at today's rate repays a different amount of money than was taken** — a guest who paid 100 USD at 3.67 and is refunded at 3.72 gets back more AED than they gave, and the venue carries the difference on every refund.
The exposure runs both ways and neither direction is defensible: a guest short-changed by a moving rate has a complaint the venue cannot answer, because **the guest did nothing but wait.**

taxReversalEntryId.description:
**A refund reverses the tax entry it created, and this is where that is stated rather than implied.** `reverseJournalEntry` and `calculateTax` both exist, so both halves were present and the obligation was assumed — **an implied obligation is one a developer can miss without failing anything.**
Null only where the original sale carried no tax.

settleTo.description:
BL-086. **A refund could only go back the way it came.** A guest whose card has expired, a partner settling by wire, a guest who would rather have the credit — three real cases with one answer.
**`originalTender` stays the default** because refunding elsewhere is how money laundering works, and anything else needs a reason.

fxVariance.description: Where the sale rate and the current rate differ, **the difference is booked as an FX variance rather than hidden in the refund**. `runFxRevaluation` already handles this class of movement and this is the same act at a smaller scale.

appliedPercentage.description: From the venue's time bands, or an approver override.

ledgerEntryId.description: Written before the gateway is called.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `venue` scope.**

bufferedSeatIds.description: Neighbours implicitly held by a seating rule.
